paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU Pro confidence vs. accuracy

annotations.annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between different accuracies and initial confidence. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence," with a linear scale ranging from approximately 0.81 to 0.99, with tick intervals at every 0.01 except 0.83. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy", also on a linear scale, with a range from 0.0 to 1.0, marked at intervals of 0.2. There are three lines: a blue solid line with square markers representing "Final Accuracy," which starts near 1.0 at an initial confidence of 0.81, maintains a relatively high level throughout, and ends slightly below 1.0 at 0.99. An orange dashed line with diamond markers represents "Δ Accuracy," starting around 0.45, showing variations throughout, and finally declining and finishing slightly above 0.0. Lastly, a green dashed line with circular markers represents "Initial Accuracy", beginning approximately 0.55 at an initial confidence of 0.81, fluctuating in value, and finally rising and ending close to 0.98. Each line visually presents changes in accuracy corresponding to initial confidence values. All three lines include error bars, indicating variability at each data point, with the blue line having the least variability for most of the data points. There are legends provided on top of the plot to match different line styles to their labels.
